title: Where the Time Goes: Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline
summary: A GPU can do arithmetic hundreds of times faster than it can fetch the numbers to do it on. This lesson counts the FLOPs and bytes of a forward pass, introduces arithmetic intensity and the roofline model, and explains why prefill is compute-bound while decode is limited by memory bandwidth.
objectives: Estimate the FLOPs per token of a transformer as about 2N and add the attention term
Estimate decode time per token from weight bytes and memory bandwidth for a 7-8B model
Compute arithmetic intensity and locate a workload on the roofline of a given GPU
Explain why prefill is compute-bound and decode is bandwidth-bound, and what batching changes
Measure efficiency with model FLOPs utilisation (MFU) and memory bandwidth utilisation (MBU)
prerequisites: You should know how a transformer block is built and roughly where its parameters are ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)), and how the KV cache grows with context ([Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache)). The previous lesson, [Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference), defines TTFT and TPOT.
